subject: Agriculture
title: The Dust Bowl
description: A quick, practical guide to The Dust Bowl.

hook.text: In the 1930s, giant dust storms buried farms across the American plains. The sky turned black at noon.

buildup.text: Farmers had plowed up millions of acres of native grassland to plant wheat during a boom market.

discovery.text: When drought hit, there were no roots to hold the soil. Wind carried topsoil hundreds of miles.

twist.text: Dust reached New York City and Washington, D.C. Politicians couldn't ignore what farmers had warned about.

climax.text: 350,000 people fled the plains. Hugh Bennett convinced Congress to create the Soil Conservation Service.

punchline.text: America broke the land. The land broke back.

quiz.question: What caused the Dust Bowl of the 1930s?
options: Plowing native grassland left topsoil exposed to wind during drought

details.summary: The Dust Bowl of the 1930s was an ecological disaster caused by decades of aggressive plowing and drought across the American Great Plains. This topic covers the causes, devastating impacts, and conservation lessons that reshaped US agricultural policy forever.
details.whyItMatters: The Dust Bowl displaced 2.5 million people and destroyed millions of acres of topsoil. It proved that poor farming practices can trigger environmental catastrophe and remains a cautionary tale for modern agriculture.
takeaways: Deep plowing destroyed native grass root systems that held the soil together
Massive dust storms carried topsoil as far as New York City and Washington, DC
The disaster led to the creation of the Soil Conservation Service and new farm policies

faq.question: What caused the Dust Bowl?
faq.answer: Homesteaders plowed up millions of acres of native prairie grass to plant wheat. When severe drought hit in the 1930s, the exposed, root-less topsoil was swept up by wind into massive dust storms that devastated the region.

faq.question: What lessons did the Dust Bowl teach about agriculture?
faq.answer: It demonstrated that ignoring soil conservation has catastrophic consequences. The US government created the Soil Conservation Service, promoted windbreaks and cover crops, and established farm subsidies that encouraged sustainable land management.
